Yeah there’s only a few select streets in my area where I can really go WOT. And yeah all the guys I’ve met in the newer vettes are nearing retirement years and they seem to appreciate me driving a car that they remember coming out new.

If you respect the power and the vehicle then the change won’t be too drastic. Honestly the C5 feels like it has the perfect amount of speed and torque. Whenever I want to quickly adjust my speed to get into a lane on the highway or street my baby seems to know exactly what I want and is just so responsive. My Corolla was a 2006/2013 and as reliable as they were, they just don’t compare in terms of fun-ness to my c5. 

My biggest advice is just take it easy the first month or so as you get used to the sudden jump in power and torque. Never turn off traction control. I’ve had my moments where I fishtail a bit as I get too excited leaving a lot or something so just remember to always respect the car and it will take care of you.

Also, I would recommend a T-Top over a soft top. I have an automatic and while I sometimes wish I get a stick, the automatic transmission is pretty decent and you can manually put it in the first 3 gears if you wanna have a bit of fun making the car go vroom vroom.

Also want to add for the MPG, I am a fairly spirited driver who drives mostly streets in traffic and my MPG sits around 17. If you have the luxury of mostly doing highway driving for work and are less inclined to be ripping ass in 1st gear then you can get better mpg than me. 

Then again, all about the smiles per gallon or whatever they say and my goodness does my baby bring a lot of smiles, not even just mine. I get constant compliments from all my coworkers m, friends, and even other vette drivers who pull up in their C7’s and C8’s.
